claim: Cryptococcus neoformans is listed by the World Health Organization as one of four high-priority infection agents.
source: The World Health Organization has recently published the first-ever list of fungi posing threats to human health that lists Cryptococcus neoformans as one of four high-priority infection agents (World Health Organization, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2022.

claim: Cryptococcus species are responsible for 15% of global HIV/AIDS-related fatalities.
source: Cryptococcus species, which cause meningoencephalitis and acute pulmonary infections, are responsible for 15% of the global HIV/AIDS-related fatalities (Erwig and Gow, 2016; Kronstad et al., 2012), totaling an estimated 220,000 deaths per year (Iyer et al., 2021; Ngan et al., 2022; Rajasingham et al., 2017; Tugume et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Cryptococcosis has a 100% death rate if patients are left untreated.
source: Cryptococcosis has a 100% death rate if patients are left untreated, but treatment remains challenging because the number of available antifungal medications is limited.
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text without specific citation, suggesting it is based on established knowledge.

claim: Amphotericin B and azoles constitute the primary treatment options for cryptococcosis.
source: Amphotericin B (Amp B) and azoles constitute the primary treatment options, with Amp B often in combination of 5-fluorocytosine (5-FC) (Billmyre et al., 2020; Molloy et al., 2018; Spadari et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The isw1Δ mutant exhibited profound resistance to azole compounds, including fluconazole and ketoconazole.
source: The isw1Δ mutant exhibited profound resistance to azole compounds, including fluconazole (FLC), ketoconazole (KTC), 5-FC, and 5-FU, but not to the polyene compound Amp B (Figure 1a), in comparison to the wild-type and the complemented strains.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The isw1Δ mutant exhibited profound resistance to 5-FC and 5-FU.
source: The isw1Δ mutant exhibited profound resistance to azole compounds, including fluconazole (FLC), ketoconazole (KTC), 5-FC, and 5-FU, but not to the polyene compound Amp B (Figure 1a), in comparison to the wild-type and the complemented strains.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The isw1Δ mutant did not show resistance to the polyene compound Amp B.
source: The isw1Δ mutant exhibited profound resistance to azole compounds, including fluconazole (FLC), ketoconazole (KTC), 5-FC, and 5-FU, but not to the polyene compound Amp B (Figure 1a), in comparison to the wild-type and the complemented strains.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The gene expression of ISW1 remains unchanged in the presence of drugs.
source: While the gene expression of ISW1 remains unchanged in the presence of drugs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), the expression of genes important in drug resistance (Denning and Bromley, 2015), including seven genes encoding ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters (CNAG_02296, CNAG_02430, CNAG_06338, CNAG_00792, CNAG_01575, CNAG_03600, and CNAG_02764), two genes encoding efflux proteins (CNAG_03101 and CNAG_01960), and three genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters (CNAG_01674, CNAG_04898, and CNAG_06259), was significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Seven genes encoding ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters were significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant.
source: While the gene expression of ISW1 remains unchanged in the presence of drugs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), the expression of genes important in drug resistance (Denning and Bromley, 2015), including seven genes encoding ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters (CNAG_02296, CNAG_02430, CNAG_06338, CNAG_00792, CNAG_01575, CNAG_03600, and CNAG_02764), two genes encoding efflux proteins (CNAG_03101 and CNAG_01960), and three genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters (CNAG_01674, CNAG_04898, and CNAG_06259), was significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Two genes encoding efflux proteins were significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant.
source: While the gene expression of ISW1 remains unchanged in the presence of drugs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), the expression of genes important in drug resistance (Denning and Bromley, 2015), including seven genes encoding ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters (CNAG_02296, CNAG_02430, CNAG_06338, CNAG_00792, CNAG_01575, CNAG_03600, and CNAG_02764), two genes encoding efflux proteins (CNAG_03101 and CNAG_01960), and three genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters (CNAG_01674, CNAG_04898, and CNAG_06259), was significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Three genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters were significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant.
source: While the gene expression of ISW1 remains unchanged in the presence of drugs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a), the expression of genes important in drug resistance (Denning and Bromley, 2015), including seven genes encoding ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters (CNAG_02296, CNAG_02430, CNAG_06338, CNAG_00792, CNAG_01575, CNAG_03600, and CNAG_02764), two genes encoding efflux proteins (CNAG_03101 and CNAG_01960), and three genes encoding major facilitator superfamily (MFS) transporters (CNAG_01674, CNAG_04898, and CNAG_06259), was significantly elevated in expression in the FLC-treated isw1Δ mutant (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The isw1Δ mutant showed a substantial reduction in FLC levels compared to the wild-type strain.
source: The results revealed a substantial reduction in FLC levels in the isw1Δ mutant compared to the wild-type strain (Figure 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The expression of FCY1, FCY2, UGD1, and UXS1 was significantly reduced in isw1Δ when treated with 5-FC.
source: The data showed that the expression of FCY1, FCY2, UGD1, and UXS1 was significantly reduced in isw1Δ when treated with 5-FC, suggesting a reduction in 5-FC uptake and conversion to toxic 5-FU (Figure 1f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: Isw1-Flag exhibited a significant binding affinity toward the promoter regulatory regions of many genes associated with drug resistance.
source: The results revealed that the Isw1-Flag exhibited a significant binding affinity toward the promoter regulatory regions of many genes associated with drug resistance (Figure 1g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Truncation of DBD, SNF2, or helicase C domains significantly impaired Isw1 function.
source: We thereby generated truncation mutant alleles for these domains, specifically DBD, SNF2, or helicase C. The results showed that Isw1 function is significantly impaired (Figure 1h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1h.

claim: Truncation mutant strains exhibited significant resistance to drug compounds.
source: Consistently, these truncation mutant strains exhibited significant resistance to the drug compounds, indicating the critical role of these domains in mediating Isw1 function (Figure 1h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1h.

claim: A total of 22 proteins interacted with Isw1-Flag.
source: We have found a total of 22 proteins that interacted with Isw1-Flag, and 11 are anticipated to be involved in the Isw1 network (Figure 2a), as shown by the STRING database (https://version-11-5.string-db.org).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry analysis data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Itc1 was observed to engage in protein–protein interactions with Isw1 in C. neoformans.
source: Similar to that of S. cerevisiae, Itc1 was also observed to engage in protein–protein interactions in C. neoformans (Figure 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: The Chd1 homolog was found to co-immunoprecipitate with Isw1 in C. neoformans.
source: Nevertheless, the Chd1 homolog was found to co-immunoprecipitate with Isw1 in C. neoformans, whereas the Sua7 homolog did not exhibit the same manners (Figure 2c).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The Sua7 homolog did not co-immunoprecipitate with Isw1 in C. neoformans.
source: Nevertheless, the Chd1 homolog was found to co-immunoprecipitate with Isw1 in C. neoformans, whereas the Sua7 homolog did not exhibit the same manners (Figure 2c).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: itc1Δ cells were resistant to antifungal agents.
source: We created the mutants of itc1Δ and chd1Δ (Figure 2d, e) and found that itc1Δ cells were resistant to antifungal agents, but the chd1Δ strain demonstrated only limited drug resistance, which are not comparable to those observed in isw1Δ cells (Figure 2d, e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d and 2e.

claim: The chd1Δ strain demonstrated only limited drug resistance.
source: We created the mutants of itc1Δ and chd1Δ (Figure 2d, e) and found that itc1Δ cells were resistant to antifungal agents, but the chd1Δ strain demonstrated only limited drug resistance, which are not comparable to those observed in isw1Δ cells (Figure 2d, e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2d and 2e.

claim: Total Isw1 protein levels are not affected by external stress inducers.
source: We gathered the evidence that total Isw1 protein levels are not affected by external stress inducers (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The isw1Δ strain did not exhibit any growth impairment when subjected to stresses such as changes in body temperature, osmotic stress, and stresses affecting the cell wall and membrane.
source: In addition, we observed that the isw1Δ strain did not exhibit any growth impairment when subjected to stresses, such as changes in body temperature, osmotic stress, and stresses affecting the cell wall and membrane (Figure 3a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: A minor impairment in melanin production was observed in the isw1Δ strain.
source: Moreover, a minor impairment in melanin production was observed, but no noticeable abnormalities in the development of the capsule were identified (Figure 3b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b and 3c.

claim: No noticeable abnormalities in the development of the capsule were identified in the isw1Δ strain.
source: Moreover, a minor impairment in melanin production was observed, but no noticeable abnormalities in the development of the capsule were identified (Figure 3b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b and 3c.

claim: No statistically significant changes in the survival rates and colony-forming units (14-day post infection) were observed among the wild-type, isw1Δ, and ISW1 complemented strains.
source: The results revealed no statistically significant changes in the survival rates and colony-forming units (CFUs) (14-day post infection) among the wild-type, isw1Δ, and ISW1 complemented strains (Figure 3d, e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3d and 3e.

claim: The isw1Δ strain exhibits enhanced fungal burdens when treated with both FLC and 5-FC in vivo.
source: Pulmonary CFU quantification revealed that the isw1Δ strain exhibits enhanced fungal burdens when treated with both drugs (Figure 3e). This enhancement is statistically significant, as indicated by the p-values of less than 0.0001 (p < 0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The Isw1-Flag fusion protein stability decreased gradually in concentration- and time-dependent manner upon exposure to FLC.
source: Using cycloheximide to inhibit protein synthesis, the Isw1-Flag fusion protein stability was found to decrease gradually in concentration- and time-dependent manner upon exposure to FLC (Figure 4a, b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a and 4b.

claim: A reduction of 50% in Isw1-Flag levels was observed 30 min after FLC exposure.
source: Specifically, a reduction of 50% was observed 30 min after FLC exposure.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: 5-FC exposure reduced Isw1-Flag levels.
source: Similarly, 5-FC exposure also reduced Isw1-Flag levels (Figure 4c, d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4c and 4d.

claim: Isw1 is ubiquitinated at 15 sites.
source: Consistent with our hypothesis, Isw1 is ubiquitinated (Figure 4e) at 15 sites (Figure 4f).
evidence: The claim is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4e and 4f.

claim: The presence of antifungal agents strongly repressed acetylation levels of Isw1.
source: The presence of antifungal agents strongly repressed acetylation levels, in contrast to deacetylation inhibitors trichostatin A (TSA) and nicotinamide (NAM), which enhanced acetylation levels (Figure 5a, b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a and 5b.

claim: Deacetylation inhibitors trichostatin A (TSA) and nicotinamide (NAM) enhanced acetylation levels of Isw1.
source: The presence of antifungal agents strongly repressed acetylation levels, in contrast to deacetylation inhibitors trichostatin A (TSA) and nicotinamide (NAM), which enhanced acetylation levels (Figure 5a, b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a and 5b.

claim: Cells with three R mutations demonstrated drug-resistant growth phenotypes similar to those of the isw1Δ strain.
source: Of the triple-mutated strains, cells with three R mutations demonstrated drug-resistant growth phenotypes that were similar to those of the isw1Δ strain, whereas those with three Q mutations showed the wild-type growth in the presence of antifungal drugs (Figure 5c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Cells with three Q mutations showed wild-type growth in the presence of antifungal drugs.
source: Of the triple-mutated strains, cells with three R mutations demonstrated drug-resistant growth phenotypes that were similar to those of the isw1Δ strain, whereas those with three Q mutations showed the wild-type growth in the presence of antifungal drugs (Figure 5c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The ISW1K97R strain showed robust resistance to antifungal drugs, mimicking the isw1Δ strain.
source: Of the strains that have single-R mutation, the ISW1K97R strain showed robust resistance to antifungal drugs, mimicking the isw1Δ strain (Figure 5d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The ISW1K97Q strain showed no drug resistance.
source: Interestingly, the ISW1K97Q strain showed no drug resistance (Figure 5—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Triple-R mutation resulted in a significant reduction in levels of Isw1-Flag.
source: To further investigate how Isw1 degradation correlates with drug resistance of C. neoformans, we tested how Isw1K97 acetylation affects its degradation using the immunoblotting method, and the results showed that triple-R mutation resulted in a significant reduction in levels of Isw1-Flag.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblotting data described in the text.

claim: Triple-Q mutation resulted in Isw1-Flag levels comparable to wild-type strains.
source: Meanwhile, triple-Q mutation resulted in Isw1-Flag levels comparable to wild-type strains (Figure 5e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5e.

claim: The single site mutant, ISW1K97R, showed a lower level of Isw1-Flag.
source: Similarly, the single site mutant, ISW1K97R, showed a lower level of Isw1-Flag (Figure 5f).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Protein levels of wild-type Isw1 and mutated Isw1K97R gradually diminished over time.
source: Moreover, protein levels of wild-type Isw1 and mutated Isw1K97R gradually diminished over time. While those of Isw1K97Q remained constant (Figure 5g–i), a faster degradation was observed for Isw1K97R (Figure 5j).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g-j.

claim: Protein levels of Isw1K97Q remained constant over time.
source: Moreover, protein levels of wild-type Isw1 and mutated Isw1K97R gradually diminished over time. While those of Isw1K97Q remained constant (Figure 5g–i), a faster degradation was observed for Isw1K97R (Figure 5j).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5g-i.

claim: A faster degradation was observed for Isw1K97R compared to wild-type Isw1.
source: Moreover, protein levels of wild-type Isw1 and mutated Isw1K97R gradually diminished over time. While those of Isw1K97Q remained constant (Figure 5g–i), a faster degradation was observed for Isw1K97R (Figure 5j).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5j.

claim: Rapamycin and MG132 promote Isw1-Flag levels.
source: Immunoblotting results showed that rapamycin and MG132 promote Isw1-Flag levels, with rapamycin's effect less prominent than MG132 (Figure 6a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Rapamycin's effect on promoting Isw1-Flag levels is less prominent than MG132.
source: Immunoblotting results showed that rapamycin and MG132 promote Isw1-Flag levels, with rapamycin's effect less prominent than MG132 (Figure 6a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Isw1-Flag protein levels were unaffected in cells treated with MG132 and FLC.
source: Cells treated with MG132 and FLC or 5-FC yielded slightly different results. Isw1-Flag protein levels were unaffected in cells treated with FLC, but the levels were reduced with 5-FC (Figure 6b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Isw1-Flag protein levels were reduced in cells treated with MG132 and 5-FC.
source: Cells treated with MG132 and FLC or 5-FC yielded slightly different results. Isw1-Flag protein levels were unaffected in cells treated with FLC, but the levels were reduced with 5-FC (Figure 6b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: MG132 treatment results in a more robust enhancement in Isw1K97R-Flag levels.
source: Given that K97 deacetylation could trigger hyper-ubiquitination of Isw1, we analyzed Isw1 ubiquitination sites and their regulation mechanisms by K97 acetylation levels and found that MG132 treatment results in a more robust enhanced in Isw1K97R-Flag levels (Figure 6d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: ISW1K113R and ISW1K441R mutations exhibited reduced drug-resistant growth of the ISW1K97R strain.
source: Only ISW1K113R and ISW1K441R mutations exhibited reduced drug-resistant growth of the ISW1K97R stain (Figure 6e), indicating that they affect drug resistance by modulating Isw1 protein stability in the absence of acetylation at the K97.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Robust elevations in Isw1-Flag levels were detected in Isw1K97R, K113R (5.6-fold) and Isw1K97R, K441R (14.5-fold).
source: The immunoblotting analysis further showed that, while all ubiquitination mutants exhibited moderately enhanced Isw1-Flag levels (Figure 6f, g), robust elevations were detected in Isw1K97R, K113R (5.6-fold) and Isw1K97R, K441R (14.5-fold) (Figure 6f, g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6f and 6g.

claim: Cdc4 is an E3 ligase for Isw1.
source: To analyze the molecular mechanism by which Isw1K97 regulates the ubiquitin–proteasome process, we generated nine knockout mutants of E3 ligase encoding genes in the genetic background of ISW1K97R and identified that Cdc4 is an E3 ligase for Isw1 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1a and Figure 7a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1a and Figure 7a.

claim: The ISW1K97R/cdc4∆ strain becomes sensitive to antifungal agents.
source: We found that the ISW1K97R/cdc4∆ strain becomes sensitive to antifungal agents (Figure 7a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: Disrupting CDC4 in the H99 strain does not affect the growth of cells in response to antifungal drugs.
source: In addition, disrupting CDC4 in the H99 strain does not affect the growth of cells in response to antifungal drugs (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Immunoblotting showed a strong elevation in Isw1K97R-Flag levels in the ISW1K97R/cdc4∆ strain.
source: Immunoblotting showed a strong elevation in Isw1K97R-Flag levels in the ISW1K97R/cdc4∆ strain (Figure 7b), in contrast to the ISW1K97R/fwd1∆ strain (Figure 7c), suggesting a potential interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Cdc4-HA co-precipitates with Isw1-Flag.
source: We then performed a co-IP assay and found that Cdc4-HA co-precipitates with Isw1-Flag (Figure 7d).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7d.

claim: There is an interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97R.
source: We also carried out co-IP to examine interactions between Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97R and Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97Q, and the results showed an interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97R but a reduction in the strength of the interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97Q, indicating the acetylation of Isw1K97 hinders its binding of the Cdc4 E3 ligase (Figure 7e).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: There is a reduction in the strength of the interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97Q.
source: We also carried out co-IP to examine interactions between Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97R and Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97Q, and the results showed an interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97R but a reduction in the strength of the interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97Q, indicating the acetylation of Isw1K97 hinders its binding of the Cdc4 E3 ligase (Figure 7e).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: The acetylation of Isw1K97 hinders its binding of the Cdc4 E3 ligase.
source: We also carried out co-IP to examine interactions between Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97R and Cdc4-HA and Isw1K97Q, and the results showed an interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97R but a reduction in the strength of the interaction between Cdc4 and Isw1K97Q, indicating the acetylation of Isw1K97 hinders its binding of the Cdc4 E3 ligase (Figure 7e).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: A total of 12 clinical isolates exhibited significant resistance to at least one antifungal drug.
source: Among them, a total of 12 isolates (CDLC4, CDLC13, CDLC15, CDLC25, CDLC60, CDLC61, CDLC62, CDLC98, CDLC125, CDLC135, CDLC141, and CDLC150) exhibited significant resistance to at least one antifungal drug.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data described in the text.

claim: PCR in conjunction with sequencing analysis yielded results indicating the absence of mutations in the drug-resistance genes of these clinical isolates.
source: It is noteworthy that the application of PCR in conjunction with sequencing analysis has yielded results indicating the absence of mutations in the drug-resistance genes of these clinical isolates (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by PCR and sequencing data referenced in Supplementary file 5.

claim: Six isolates demonstrated no resistance to antifungal agents.
source: Conversely, six isolates (CDLC120, CDLC6, CDLC27, CDLC37, CDLC43, and CDLC100) demonstrated no resistance to antifungal agents, and their growth patterns resembled that of the H99 strain in the presence of these drugs (Figure 8—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Strains that displayed phenotypes of multidrug resistance exhibited notably diminished levels of Isw1-Flag.
source: The protein expression results exhibited three distinct classes: (1) Strains that displayed phenotypes of multidrug resistance exhibited notably diminished levels of Isw1-Flag. These strains include CDLC15, CDLC25, CDLC61, CDLC62, and CDLC98.
evidence: The claim is supported by protein expression data described in the text.

claim: Strains that exhibited sensitivity to drug treatment displayed robust protein levels of Isw1-Flag.
source: (2) Conversely, strains that exhibited sensitivity to drug treatment displayed robust protein levels of Isw1-Flag. Notable examples of such strains are CDCL120, CDCLC6, CDCL37, CDCLC43, and CDLC100.
evidence: The claim is supported by protein expression data described in the text.

claim: Drug-resistant strains demonstrated Isw1-Flag levels comparable to those of the H99 strain.
source: (3) Drug-resistant strains demonstrated Isw1-Flag levels comparable to those of the H99 strain. This similarity was observed in strains such as CDCL141 and CDLC4 (Figure 8a and Figure 8—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a and Figure 8—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The changes in Isw1-Flag levels observed were not attributed to transcriptional modifications.
source: Significantly, the changes in Isw1-Flag levels observed were not attributed to transcriptional modifications (Figure 8—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Samples derived from three distinct clinical isolates revealed heightened levels of Isw1 upon exposure to MG132.
source: In a manner akin to PTMs observed in Isw1 from the H99 strain, our analysis of samples derived from three distinct clinical isolates revealed heightened levels of Isw1 upon exposure to MG132 (Figure 8b, c).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8b and 8c.

claim: The clinical isolates that were subjected to TSA and NAM treatment exhibited enhanced levels of Isw1 acetylation.
source: Furthermore, the clinical isolates that were subjected to TSA and NAM treatment exhibited enhanced levels of Isw1 acetylation, as demonstrated in (Figure 8d).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8d.

claim: The H99 strain revealed a decrease in cell growth when the ISW1K97Q gene was overexpressed in the presence of antifungal drugs.
source: Initially, the H99 strain was subjected to testing, which revealed a decrease in cell growth when the ISW1K97Q gene was overexpressed in the presence of antifungal drugs (Figure 8e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8e.

claim: All four clinical strains overexpressing ISW1K97Q displayed a susceptible cell growth response to antifungal drugs.
source: Subsequently, four strains, namely CDLC120, CDLC141, CDLC135, and CDLC61, were subjected to transformation and subsequent testing. The results indicated that all four clinical strains overexpressing ISW1K97Q displayed a susceptible cell growth response to antifungal drugs (Figure 8f–i).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8f-i.

claim: The CDLC135 ISW1K97Q strain exhibited a sensitive growth pattern toward azoles but demonstrated a resistant growth phenotype when exposed to 5-FC.
source: Conversely, the CDLC135 ISW1K97Q strain exhibited a sensitive growth pattern toward azoles but demonstrated a resistant growth phenotype when exposed to 5-FC (Figure 8g).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8g.

claim: An elevation in Isw1 level was found to suppress the growth of drug resistance in the CDLC141 strain.
source: While the Isw1 level remains constant in CDLC141, an elevation in Isw1 level was found to suppress the growth of drug resistance in this strain (Figure 8h).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8h.

claim: Isw1 is a master regulator of multidrug responses in both laboratory and clinical strains.
source: Taken together, our evidence demonstrates the critical function of Isw1 as a master regulator of multidrug responses in both laboratory and clinical strains.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Approximately 300 million people suffer from fungal-related diseases, subsequently leading to 1.6 million deaths annually.
source: It is estimated that approximately 300 million people suffer from fungal-related diseases, subsequently leading to 1.6 million deaths annually (Stop neglecting fungi, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Certain pathogenic fungi are linked with cancer development.
source: Intriguingly, certain pathogenic fungi are linked with cancer development (Hosseini et al., 2022; Narunsky-Haziza et al., 2022; Saftien et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Cryptococcus is involved in secondary infections in people with COVID-19.
source: Recently, it has been reported that Cryptococcus is also involved in secondary infections in people with COVID-19 (Khatib et al., 2021; Spadari et al., 2020; Woldie et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The US FDA has categorized anti-cryptococcal therapies as 'orphan drugs'.
source: In light of the treatment limitations and risks, as well as the high costs associated with developing new antifungal treatments, the US FDA has categorized anti-cryptococcal therapies as 'orphan drugs', granting regulatory support by reducing the requirements for clinical studies (Denning and Bromley, 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Point mutations in binding domains or regions of the drug target proteins often hinder their interactions with drugs resulting in resistance.
source: Point mutations in binding domains or regions of the drug target proteins often hinder their interactions with drugs resulting in resistance (Sionov et al., 2012; Wan et al., 2021), such as in the case of lanosterol demethylase, encoded by the ERG11 gene, in Candida and Cryptococcus species (Bosco-Borgeat et al., 2016; Sionov et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Defects in DNA mismatch repairs resulting in high gene mutation rates and, thereby, 5-FC resistance was identified in C. deuterogattii.
source: Defects in DNA mismatch repairs resulting in high gene mutation rates and, thereby, 5-FC resistance was identified in C. deuterogattii, a species distinct but close to C. neoformans (Billmyre et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Mutations in genes encoding the cytosine permease (Fcy2), uracil phosphoribosyl transferase (Fur1), and UDP-glucuronic acid decarboxylase (Uxs1) conferring 5-FC resistance were identified in multiple clinical cryptococcal isolates.
source: Mutations in genes encoding the cytosine permease (Fcy2), uracil phosphoribosyl transferase (Fur1), and UDP-glucuronic acid decarboxylase (Uxs1) conferring 5-FC resistance were also identified in multiple clinical cryptococcal isolates (Billmyre et al., 2020; Chang et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Studies of C. albicans transcription factor Tac1 illustrate that gain-of-function mutations or alterations in gene copy numbers regulate efflux pump genes.
source: Studies of C. albicans transcription factor Tac1 illustrate that gain-of-function mutations or alterations in gene copy numbers regulate efflux pump genes (Coste et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Gain-of-function mutations were identified in C. albicans transcription factors Upc2 and Mrr1, which activate ERG11 gene expression and drug pumps, respectively.
source: Gain-of-function mutations were also identified in C. albicans transcription factors Upc2 and Mrr1, which activate ERG11 gene expression and drug pumps, respectively (Dunkel et al., 2008; Silver et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: A Upc2 homolog was identified in C. neoformans to be involved in regulating steroid biosynthesis.
source: A Upc2 homolog was identified in C. neoformans to be involved in regulating steroid biosynthesis, but its role in drug resistance was not clear (Kim et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The acetylation of the heat-shock protein Hsp90 mediates antifungal drug response in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and C. albicans by blocking the interaction between Hsp90 and calcineurin.
source: The acetylation of the heat-shock protein Hsp90 mediates antifungal drug response in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and C. albicans by blocking the interaction between Hsp90 and calcineurin (Robbins et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The ISWI has a highly conserved ATPase domain from the SWI2/SNF2 family, which belongs to the superfamily of DEAD/H-helicases.
source: The ISWI has a highly conserved ATPase domain from the SWI2/SNF2 family, which belongs to the superfamily of DEAD/H-helicases.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about ISWI protein structure.

claim: The ISWI–ACF complex in Neurospora crassa is essential for repressing a certain set of genes that have been methylated at the H3K27, as well as genes targeted by PRC2 (polycomb repressed complex 2).
source: The ISWI–ACF complex in Neurospora crassa is essential for repressing a certain set of genes that have been methylated at the H3K27, as well as genes targeted by PRC2 (polycomb repressed complex 2) (Kamei et al., 2021; Wiles et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The baker's yeast contains two similar versions of Isws, known as Isw1 and Isw2.
source: The baker's yeast contains two similar versions of Isws, known as Isw1 and Isw2.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about S. cerevisiae.

claim: Isw1 forms associations with either Ioc3 or Ioc2 and Ioc4 to create two separate remodeling complexes, known as Isw1a and Isw1b, respectively.
source: Isw1 forms associations with either Ioc3 or Ioc2 and Ioc4 to create two separate remodeling complexes, known as Isw1a and Isw1b, respectively (Vary et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The S. cerevisiae Isw2 protein has the capability to interact with Itc1, forming a complex that can position the remodeler during the process of nucleosome sliding.
source: The S. cerevisiae Isw2 protein has the capability to interact with Itc1, forming a complex that can position the remodeler during the process of nucleosome sliding (Kagalwala et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The Isw1b complex acts in conjugation with Chd1 to regulate chromatin organization.
source: For instance, the Isw1b complex acts in conjugation with Chd1 to regulate chromatin organization (Smolle et al., 2012), and the ability of Isw2 to attach to DNA might be dependent on Sua7 (Yadon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: The ability of Isw2 to attach to DNA might be dependent on Sua7.
source: For instance, the Isw1b complex acts in conjugation with Chd1 to regulate chromatin organization (Smolle et al., 2012), and the ability of Isw2 to attach to DNA might be dependent on Sua7 (Yadon et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation.

claim: Transcriptome analysis revealed 1275 genes, approximately 18.3% of the genome, that were significantly differentially expressed in the isw1Δ mutant when treated with FLC.
source: In C. neoformans, transcriptome analysis revealed 1275 genes, approximately 18.3% of the genome, that were significantly differentially expressed in the isw1Δ mutant when treated with FLC.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data.

claim: The changes in gene expression had a significant impact on the drug efflux system through the activation of 12 drug pump genes and the repression of 9 pump genes.
source: The changes in gene expression had a significant impact on the drug efflux system through the activation of 12 drug pump genes and the repression of 9 pump genes, which included ABC and MFS transporter genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptome analysis data.

claim: Isw1 represses genes responsible for resistance to FLC.
source: While Isw1 represses genes responsible for resistance to FLC, it also positively modulates the expression of genes required for 5-FC resistance, implying that chromatin remodeling of Isw1 is necessary as the cell responds to disparate chemical stresses and that Isw1 engages distinct remodeling venues to overcome drug toxicity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data and discussion.

claim: Isw1 positively modulates the expression of genes required for 5-FC resistance.
source: While Isw1 represses genes responsible for resistance to FLC, it also positively modulates the expression of genes required for 5-FC resistance, implying that chromatin remodeling of Isw1 is necessary as the cell responds to disparate chemical stresses and that Isw1 engages distinct remodeling venues to overcome drug toxicity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data and discussion.

claim: The overall abundance of Isw1 remains constant in response to external stimuli.
source: The overall abundance of Isw1 remains constant in response to external stimuli, and alterations in Isw1 protein levels may change when protein synthesis is inhibited, due to the interplay between two PTMs.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The isw1Δ strain exhibited the ability to endure stresses.
source: Nevertheless, the investigations on the growth of cells demonstrated that the isw1Δ strain exhibited the ability to endure stresses, so indicating that Isw1 does not regulate fungal virulence factors and pathogenicity.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: Isw1 does not regulate fungal virulence factors and pathogenicity.
source: Nevertheless, the investigations on the growth of cells demonstrated that the isw1Δ strain exhibited the ability to endure stresses, so indicating that Isw1 does not regulate fungal virulence factors and pathogenicity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing no difference in virulence.

claim: The isw1Δ strain displayed notable resistance to antifungal treatments both in vitro condition and in animal models.
source: However, the isw1Δ strain displayed notable resistance to antifungal treatments both in vitro condition and in animal models.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from in vitro and in vivo studies.

claim: The total acetylation levels of Isw1 were reduced when cells were treated with FLC or 5-FC.
source: The total acetylation levels of Isw1 were reduced when cells were treated with FLC or 5-FC, leading to the activation of Isw1 ubiquitination machinery.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data.

claim: The K97 acetylation site functions as the essential regulating component of the interplay between acetylation and ubiquitination.
source: We identified that the K97 acetylation site functions as the essential regulating component of this interplay.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis studies.

claim: K97 acetylation acts as a switch for ubiquitin conjugation proceeding proteasome-mediated degradation.
source: We also found that K97 acetylation acts as a switch for ubiquitin conjugation proceeding proteasome-mediated degradation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis and degradation studies.

claim: When deacetylated, K97 triggers the activation of Isw1 degradation via the ubiquitin–proteasome process.
source: When deacetylated, K97 triggers the activation of Isw1 degradation via the ubiquitin–proteasome process (acetylated K97 blocks the physical interaction with Cdc4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis and co-IP studies.

claim: Acetylated K97 blocks the physical interaction with Cdc4.
source: When deacetylated, K97 triggers the activation of Isw1 degradation via the ubiquitin–proteasome process (acetylated K97 blocks the physical interaction with Cdc4).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-IP experimental data.

claim: Isw1 could be modulated by other proteins, such as another uncharacterized E3 ligase.
source: These data suggested that Isw1 could also be modulated by other proteins, such as another uncharacterized E3 ligase.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the observation that cdc4Δ does not fully restore sensitivity.

claim: The K113 site may undergo acetylation or ubiquitination modifications.
source: Interestingly, the K113 site may undergo acetylation or ubiquitination modifications, whereas the K441 site undergoes only ubiquitination.
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry data identifying both modifications at K113.

claim: The K441 site undergoes only ubiquitination.
source: Interestingly, the K113 site may undergo acetylation or ubiquitination modifications, whereas the K441 site undergoes only ubiquitination.
evidence: The claim is based on mass spectrometry data identifying ubiquitination at K441.

claim: Isw1K113 and Isw1K441 provide a predominant role in regulating the ubiquitin-proteasome process of Isw1.
source: Collectively, these results showed that Isw1K113 and Isw1K441 provide a predominant role in regulating the ubiquitin-proteasome process of Isw1 and that acetylation at Isw1K97 has a broad role in controlling the ubiquitination process at those sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from ubiquitination site mutagenesis studies.

claim: Acetylation at Isw1K97 has a broad role in controlling the ubiquitination process at K113 and K441 sites.
source: Collectively, these results showed that Isw1K113 and Isw1K441 provide a predominant role in regulating the ubiquitin-proteasome process of Isw1 and that acetylation at Isw1K97 has a broad role in controlling the ubiquitination process at those sites.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from mutagenesis studies.

claim: Both degradation pathways (autophagy and proteasomal) are utilized in Isw1-Flag degradation.
source: These findings suggested that both degradation pathways are utilized in Isw1-Flag degradation, but the ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal process has a more predominant role.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data using rapamycin and MG132.

claim: The ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal process has a more predominant role in Isw1 degradation.
source: These findings suggested that both degradation pathways are utilized in Isw1-Flag degradation, but the ubiquitin-mediated proteasomal process has a more predominant role.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing MG132 has a stronger effect than rapamycin.

claim: The acetylation–Isw1–ubiquitination regulatory axis represents a naturally occurring mechanism employed to modulate multidrug resistance in clinical strains of C. neoformans.
source: Hence, the acetylation–Isw1–ubiquitination regulatory axis represents a naturally occurring mechanism employed to modulate multidrug resistance in clinical strains of C. neoformans.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data from clinical isolates.

claim: The control of Isw1 in drug resistance relies on the Isw1–Itc1 complex.
source: Therefore, these findings indicate that the control of Isw1 in drug resistance relies on the Isw1–Itc1 complex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that itc1Δ shows drug resistance similar to isw1Δ.

claim: Isw1 may potentially carry out its function through alternative complex regulatory networks.
source: However, given the presence of other Isw1-interacting proteins in our data, it is possible that Isw1 may potentially carry out its function through alternative complex regulatory networks.
evidence: The claim is speculative based on the identification of multiple Isw1-interacting proteins.

claim: Isw1 plays a pivotal role as a key regulator of drug resistance, both in vivo and in vitro.
source: These data thus provided substantial evidence supporting the pivotal role of Isw1 as a key regulator of drug resistance, both in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on experimental data from in vitro and in vivo studies.

claim: C. neoformans actively reduces Isw1 protein levels through protein degradation in the presence of antifungal drugs.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrated that C. neoformans actively reduces Isw1 protein levels through protein degradation in the presence of antifungal drugs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on experimental data showing time- and concentration-dependent degradation.

claim: The ubiquitination machinery of Isw1 is actively initiated during drug exposure.
source: These results indicated that the ubiquitination machinery of Isw1 is actively initiated during drug exposure, and this, in turn, decreases Isw1 protein levels and hinders Isw1 transcription repression of genes for drug resistance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of ubiquitination and degradation upon drug exposure.

claim: There exists an interplay network simultaneously controlling Isw1 stability in response to antifungal drugs.
source: The finding of Isw1 subject to ubiquitination and acetylation regulation also suggested that there exists an interplay network simultaneously controlling Isw1 stability in response to antifungal drugs.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of both acetylation and ubiquitination modifications.

claim: The acetylation status of Isw1K97 plays a critical role in regulating Isw1 protein stability and function in response to antifungal drugs.
source: Collectively, these data strongly demonstrated that the acetylation status of Isw1K97 plays a critical role in regulating Isw1 protein stability and function in response to antifungal drugs.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on mutagenesis and protein stability studies.

claim: Acetylation at K97 blocked the degradation of Isw1.
source: Therefore, Isw1K97 is an essential regulation site responsible for Isw1 stability; that is, acetylation at K97 blocked the degradation of Isw1, and deacetylation at K97 facilitated Isw1 degradation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on protein stability studies of K97 mutants.

claim: Deacetylation at K97 facilitated Isw1 degradation.
source: Therefore, Isw1K97 is an essential regulation site responsible for Isw1 stability; that is, acetylation at K97 blocked the degradation of Isw1, and deacetylation at K97 facilitated Isw1 degradation.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on protein stability studies of K97 mutants.

claim: The chromatin remodeler Isw1 plays a pivotal role as a primary regulator of antifungal drug resistance in C. neoformans through the direct interaction of Isw1 with its target genes and subsequently alteration of gene expression.
source: Collectively, these data strongly supported the proposition that the chromatin remodeler Isw1 plays a pivotal role as a primary regulator of antifungal drug resistance in C. neoformans. This regulatory function is achieved through the direct interaction of Isw1 with its target genes and subsequently alteration of gene expression.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on ChIP-PCR and truncation studies.

claim: The modulation of drug pumps by Isw1 is subject to the influence of FLC.
source: The evidence presented indicates that the modulation of drug pumps by Isw1 is subject to the influence of FLC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from transcriptome data comparing FLC-treated and untreated conditions.

claim: Isw1 plays a crucial role in regulating the drug efflux mechanism during drug treatment.
source: The data collectively indicate that Isw1 plays a crucial role in regulating the drug efflux mechanism during drug treatment.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on transcriptome and intracellular drug concentration data.

claim: The strong drug-resistance phenotype observed in the isw1Δ strain may be attributed to the concurrent modulation of gene expression of multiple drug pumps.
source: The results presented suggests that the strong drug-resistance phenotype observed in the isw1Δ strain may be attributed to the concurrent modulation of gene expression of multiple drug pumps, which subsequently facilitate the active removal of intracellular drug molecules.
evidence: The claim is inferred from transcriptome and intracellular drug concentration data.

claim: Isw1 is a master transcriptional regulator of drug-resistance genes in C. neoformans.
source: These data suggested that Isw1 is a master transcriptional regulator of drug-resistance genes in C. neoformans.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion based on transcriptome and qRT-PCR data.

claim: The regulatory mechanisms of the cryptococcal ISW1 complex in drug resistance are mediated by the Isw1–Itc1 regulatory axis, rather than the Isw1–Chd1 pathway.
source: This finding provides additional evidence that the regulatory mechanisms of the cryptococcal ISW1 complex in drug resistance are mediated by the Isw1–Itc1 regulatory axis, rather than the Isw1–Chd1 pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that itc1Δ shows drug resistance but chd1Δ does not.
